summary: Projects run together to bring about one change.
example: Quality Improvement Programme, which runs its projects, such as the Quality Check Rollout, together towards one quality standard.

theory of change.summary: How a programme expects its projects' results to add up to the change it wants: each step, what must be true before it, and why it follows.
theory of change.example: Depot staff apply the standard alike, so faults are found before produce leaves, so produce meets one standard, if depots release staff for training.

definition: A programme is a set of related projects, and smaller programmes, run together to bring about one change and the benefits it brings. Each project is a step that change needs, and the programme says how the steps lead to it. The programme records the change it wants, the problems it solves, the outcomes and measures it is judged on, how its steps lead to the change, its own risks and who runs it. Each project, smaller programme or operation in it names the programme itself. A programme is not a portfolio (work grouped to decide what to fund, which need not depend on one another), not a project (work with a start and an end, one person in charge and one budget), not an operation (work that keeps running), and not a goal (an aim in your strategy).

cues.programme: related projects coordinated together towards one shared change

/metadata/name.guide: The name people use for the programme, not for the work inside it.

poor.why: Names two projects, not the programme that runs them.
A code, not a name. Put the code in the alias.

/spec/aim/change.guide: What is true once the programme succeeds, not the work that gets there. Leave numbers to the measures. If you quote the aim from a published document, copy all of it here word for word.
good: Every depot checks produce against one published standard.
A larger share of each season reaches retail buyers directly, on terms the cooperative sets.

poor.text: Run training for depot staff and roll out the quality check tool to every depot.
poor.why: Describes the work. Say what will be different once the work is done.

poor.text: Raise the quality pass rate to 90% by 2027.
poor.why: A target, not a change. Put the figure and date on a measure.
A topic, not a change: nobody could tell when it had happened.

/spec/aim/gain.guide: Who is better off once the change happens, and how. Optional.
good: Buyers get one quality from the cooperative whichever depot filled the order.
Members are paid a price they can plan around.

poor.why: Names nobody. Say which group gains.

poor.text: The quality team meets its targets.
poor.why: The team doing the work is not who the change is for; say who outside the programme is better off.

/spec/source.guide: The document that sets out the programme, with the section or page. Leave empty if it is written nowhere else.

poor.why: Not precise enough to find again: which document, and where in it?

/spec/problems.guide: The problems the programme solves. For each one: who it affects, the change that solves it, and the gaps that show it.

/spec/problems/-/groups.guide: The groups of people this problem affects. If none fits, add the group first.

poor.why: A team doing the work, not people the problem affects.

/spec/problems/-/problem/situation.guide: What the affected groups cannot do today.
good: get a different verdict on the same delivery depending on which depot checks it
learn of a failed delivery a season late

poor.text: There is no single quality standard.
poor.why: Describes a system, not people. Say what it stops the groups from doing.

poor.text: need a new quality check tool
poor.why: Names a solution. Say what the groups cannot do.

/spec/problems/-/problem/cause.guide: Why the problem happens. Fix the cause and the problem goes away.
good: each depot checks against its own checklist and none of them agree

poor.text: poor management, old equipment and a lack of training
poor.why: Three causes in one. Name the one this change fixes, and add the others as separate problems.

/spec/problems/-/change/what.guide: What is true once this problem is solved, not the work to get there.
good: Every depot checks against one published standard

poor.text: Train depot staff on the new standard
poor.why: A task for a project. Say what will be true once it is done.

/spec/problems/-/change/gain.guide: What the affected groups can do once the change happens.
good: get the same verdict on a delivery whichever depot checks it

poor.why: Not something anyone could observe; say what they can do that they could not before.

/spec/problems/-/gaps.guide: The gaps that show this problem exists, and which parts of each gap the programme covers.

/spec/problems/-/gaps/-/gap.guide: The gap that shows this problem. If it is not listed yet, add the gap first.

/spec/problems/-/gaps/-/segments.guide: Which parts of the gap this programme covers, such as places or groups. You can only pick parts the gap lists.

poor.text: A segment the gap does not name, such as a product line when the gap was observed by depot
poor.why: The gap has no evidence for that part, so Cartograph will not save it.

/spec/goals.guide: The outcomes this programme is judged on: what is true once its projects succeed. Pick outcomes, not goals or objectives. If none fits, add the outcome first.

poor.why: A goal, not an outcome. Pick the outcomes that lead to the goal.

poor.text: Every outcome its projects serve, added to look complete
poor.why: Pick only outcomes the whole programme is judged on. An outcome that one project serves belongs to that project.

/spec/kpis.guide: The measures that show whether the programme's change is happening. If none fits, add the KPI first.

poor.why: Measures whether depots stay open, not the quality change this programme wants.
Counts the work done, not the benefit. Put it on the project.

/spec/pathway.guide: How the programme's work leads to its change, step by step. Start from the change and ask what must be true first, until you reach work the projects do.

/spec/pathway/-/outcome.guide: The outcome reached at this step. Each outcome can be in one step only.

/spec/pathway/-/from.guide: The outcomes that must all be true before this one. Leave empty if the projects' work leads straight to it.

poor.text: Two outcomes listed because either one would do
poor.why: List only outcomes that must all be true. Put either-or routes in separate steps.

/spec/pathway/-/because.guide: Why those outcomes lead to this one.
good: A checker who applies the standard the same way each time catches the fault at intake instead of passing it down the line.
One published standard, and training run against it, is what makes two checkers give the same delivery the same verdict.

poor.why: Does not say how. Say how training improves quality.
Says who approved it, not why it works.

/spec/pathway/-/assumes.guide: What must be true, outside the programme's control, for this step to work. Things the programme can manage go under Risks.

poor.text: An assumption that the training budget is approved
poor.why: The programme can act on that, so it is a risk or a dependency to manage, not an assumption.

/spec/risks.guide: Risks, issues, dependencies and limits that affect the whole programme, not just one project. Add a risk to one project on that project.

/spec/risks/-/type.guide: Risk (may happen), issue (is happening), dependency (waits on something else), or constraint (a limit that is fixed).

/spec/risks/-/description.guide: What could happen or is happening, in one sentence of no more than 160 characters, specific enough to act on.
good: Depots may not release staff for training during the peak of the season.
The member register must stay current for checks to know who delivered.

poor.why: A topic, not a risk: say what could happen and to what.

poor.text: The scanner battery fails on the pilot route.
poor.why: A risk inside one project's work; it belongs on that project, not the programme.

/spec/risks/-/impact.guide: How badly it would hurt the change if it happened: low, medium or high.

/spec/risks/-/likelihood.guide: How likely it is to happen: low, medium or high. An issue is already happening.

/spec/risks/-/mitigation.guide: What will be done to make it less likely or less harmful, in one sentence of no more than 160 characters.
good: Schedule training in the two weeks before the season opens, when depots are quiet.

poor.why: Watching is not acting: say what will be done, and when.

/spec/risks/-/owner.guide: The role that watches this risk and acts on it day to day. A role, not a person. A lower-impact risk with no owner falls to the programme manager.

poor.why: A person, not a role. Pick the role the person has.
The sponsor is who you go to when a risk gets too big. The owner manages it day to day.

/spec/risks/-/depends/direction.guide: Whether this programme needs the other work, or the other work needs this programme. Record it on one side only.

/spec/risks/-/depends/on.guide: What this waits on: a programme, project, operation or data source in Cartograph, or an outside party by name.

poor.text: Market Access Programme, when that programme already declares that it needs this one
poor.why: Recorded twice, and makes a loop where neither programme can start.

/spec/risks/-/depends/needBy.guide: Leave empty. A programme has no phases.

/spec/risks/-/escalate/flag.guide: Whether this needs a decision from above the programme. Turn it on only when the programme cannot settle it itself.

/spec/risks/-/escalate/reason.guide: Why a decision is needed from above, in one sentence. Required when escalation is on.
good: Both programmes need the quality reviewer role in the same weeks, and only the sponsor can set the order.

poor.why: Says how it feels, not what decision is needed.

/spec/risks/-/escalate/to.guide: Who must decide: a role in Cartograph, or an outside body by name. Never a person.

poor.why: A person, not a role. Pick the role the person has.

/spec/sponsor.guide: The role responsible for the programme and its benefits. A role, not a person. If none fits, add the role first.

poor.why: A person, not a role. Pick the role the person has.
A team, not a role. The sponsor is one role.

/spec/manager.guide: The role that runs the programme day to day and coordinates its projects. A role, not a person.

poor.text: depot-supervisor, because the supervisor of the pilot project also runs it
poor.why: That role runs one project. Name the role that coordinates all of them.

/spec/businessChangeManager.guide: The role that makes the change last in daily work and gets the benefits once projects finish. Not the programme manager.

poor.text: The same role as the programme manager, because no one else was thought of
poor.why: Name who makes the change last in daily work, or leave empty until you know.

/spec/leadTeam.guide: The team that leads the programme. If none fits, add the team first.

poor.why: A role, not a team.

/spec/supportingTeams.guide: Other teams that do part of the programme's work.

poor.why: Name only the teams that do part of the work.

/spec/mandate.guide: What allows or requires the programme, such as a decision, policy, law, contract or request.

/spec/mandate/-/title.guide: The title of the decision or document, as it is written.
good: Approval of the quality improvement programme

poor.why: Not a title anyone could look up: give the decision's own title and its reference.

/spec/mandate/-/issuer.guide: The board, committee or role in Cartograph that issued it. If it is not there yet, add it first.
good: Sponsor, one of this work's roles

poor.why: Pick the body from the list instead of typing it.

/spec/mandate/-/issuedBy.guide: The outside body that issued it, such as a government, regulator or funder.

/spec/notes.guide: Anything else people should know about this programme.

/spec/programmes.guide: The larger programmes this one is part of. Leave empty if it is not part of another.

/spec/portfolios.guide: The portfolios that select and fund this programme, if any.

/spec/escalationRoute.guide: Who decides when the programme cannot, in order, nearest first. Leave out anyone who only receives reports.
good: Project board, then steering committee, then the national government

Project:/spec/alignment/programmes.ask: Which projects does this programme coordinate? A project names the programmes it belongs to, so open each project and choose this programme under Part of.
Project:/spec/alignment/programmes.ifNone: Add the programme first. Then add each part that has an end as a project, and choose this programme on it.

Operation:/spec/programmes.ask: Which ongoing services are part of this programme? Open each one and choose this programme.
Operation:/spec/programmes.ifNone: Add the programme first. Then add each ongoing service as an operation and choose this programme on it.

Programme:/spec/programmes.ask: Which smaller programmes are part of this one? Open each one and choose this programme.
Programme:/spec/programmes.ifNone: A smaller programme belongs here only if it works towards the same outcomes. If not, make it a separate programme.

checks.components-present: Open a project, programme or operation and choose this programme on it.
checks.problems-stated: State at least one problem the programme solves, and the change that solves it.
checks.problems-groups: Name the groups each problem affects.
checks.problems-gaps: Link each problem to the gap that shows it, or add the gap first.
checks.alignment-goals: Pick at least one outcome this programme works towards.
checks.alignment-kpis: Name at least one indicator the programme is judged by.
checks.risks-owned: Name the role that owns every high-impact risk.
checks.risks-dependency-edges: Say what each dependency waits on: something in Cartograph, or an outside party.
checks.risks-dependency-cycle: Break the loop by removing or redirecting one of the dependencies, so nothing this programme waits on is waiting on it.
checks.components-serve-outcomes: Each project in this programme should work towards one of its outcomes. If one does not, move it or add the missing outcome.
checks.aim-change: Say what will be true once the programme succeeds.
checks.pathway-steps: Add the steps from the work to the change: each outcome, what must be true first, and why it follows.
checks.governance-lead: Name the team that leads the programme.
